note:
# Census pass: P-E-2019-1902054-4ff1f32f

## What the paper is
One valuation curve for a land-use project. The ecosystem gain E(A) and the impact term
I(A) are added into a single logistic V(A), and the same function is then instantiated
three times with different coefficients: Kubuqi desert greening (positive initial system),
China Baowu steel production (negative), and the Wolong panda reserve (positive, small
scale). Seventeen physical pages, ten printed exhibits, and not one table.

## Coverage arithmetic
Ten measured regions on nine of the seventeen pages, and they close with nothing left
over: ten figure rows, zero exclusions, zero unaccounted. That is the second census in
this lane to finish on arithmetic with no non-exhibit region, after #171 - and unlike
#171, where eleven of the "figures" were grids, this paper prints no grid of any kind, so
the table-grid block is empty by fact.

## The finding: one drawing does the work of three
Figures 4, 8 and 10 are the same Excel line chart redrawn: a logistic curve on a light
grey grid that overruns every axis, a single labelled y value, two to four x ticks, no
axis titles, no legend. What changes between them is the sign and the coefficients. So
three of the ten exhibits are one plot, and the paper's evidence base is smaller than its
exhibit count suggests.

The two exhibits that are NOT model output are borrowed pictures: Figure 3, a pair of
satellite photographs of the Kubuqi dune field in 2000 and 2016, and Figure 9, a pair of
gridded suitability maps from a cited panda study. Together they occupy the two largest
regions in the paper (0.1478 and 0.2017 of a page) while every model chart is drawn at
0.065 to 0.128 - the cited pictures are printed bigger than the paper's own results.

## Geometry: annotation rails instead of legends
Half the labelling is drawn, not keyed. Figures 1 and 2 carry a three-entry legend inside
the plot AND a three-box annotation rail down the right side that explains the argument
("+E(A) +I(A) : improvement" and its two siblings). Figure 4's two blue arrows ("Value
turns positive at 2091", "Value reaches maximum at 4500") are the only numbers the chart
makes readable, and Figure 5's three boxed coordinate pairs play the same role. Figure 6
is the single conventional exhibit: a four-series stacked column with its key above the
frame and an in-plot title repeating the caption.

Two exhibits are multipanel, both 1x2, neither sharing an axis: Figure 3's photographs,
which the figure captions itself inside the frame as "Figure (a)" and "Figure (b)", and
Figure 9's two maps, which duplicate their coordinate ticks panel by panel. Figure 9 is
the only colourbar in the paper. Nothing is three-dimensional.

## Captions: ten labels, no verbs, one substitution
All ten print below their art and all ten are noun phrases or gerunds - no finite verb, no
unit, no condition, no conclusion, six to eighteen words, uniform "Figure n:" numbering.
The only caption damage in the paper is lexical: the text layer returns Figure 7's caption
as "Air pollution in Shanghui" while the page prints "Shanghai", so that row is typed from
the crop. That is a new break mode for this lane - the layer did not truncate or weld, it
substituted.

## Citation: three named, one misdirected
Only Figures 4, 5 and 8 are ever named by number. Figures 1, 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10 are never
named: Figure 6 is reached as "the stacked column chart above", Figure 9 only through the
citation that precedes it, Figure 7 not at all. And the paper's one name-drop of Figure 3
happens in the panda section, where the sentence is describing the panda study and points
at "May(Figure 3)" - the desert photograph. A reader who followed that pointer would read
the wrong exhibit, which makes this the lane's first wrong-exhibit cross-reference, as
distinct from #169's five missing pointers.

## The layer's own defects
"Shanghui" for Shanghai, "N et(A)" for Net(A) in equation (14), and a clipped x tick in
Figure 5 where the frame cuts "14" off 14000. The running head is real text ("Team 1902054"
in the layer, TEAM 1902054 as printed) and the folio runs one behind the physical page.
rules: Ten measured regions on nine of the seventeen pages, ten printed exhibits, zero exclusions and zero unaccounted: every region the pass boxes is a numbered figure, and the paper prints no region for the pass to throw away - the second census in the lane to close on arithmetic with nothing left over [place.section_path].

The paper prints TEN FIGURES AND NO TABLE AT ALL, so there is no grid, no rule style, no zebra, no merged header and no decimal column to record anywhere in it - the table-grid block of this census is empty by fact, not by omission [geometry.family].

Family mix of the ten figures: line 6 (Figures 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10), photo-or-raster-image 2 (Figures 3, 7), bar 1 (Figure 6, the only stacked column) and heatmap-or-contour 1 (Figure 9, the only gridded surface) [geometry.family].

ONE DRAWING CARRIES THE WHOLE PAPER: Figures 4, 8 and 10 are the same Excel line chart redrawn with different coefficients - a logistic curve on a grey grid, one labelled asymptote, no axis titles, no legend - so three of the ten exhibits are the same plot under three parameter sets [geometry.family].

Two exhibits are multipanel and both are 1x2: Figure 3 is a pair of satellite photographs and Figure 9 a pair of gridded suitability maps; neither shares an axis, and in Figure 9 the two panels print duplicate ticks instead [geometry.panel_count].

Legends: INSIDE the plot twice (Figures 1 and 2, each a three-entry K-sign key at upper left), ABOVE the plot once (Figure 6's four series as a colour row) and ABSENT from the other seven, where annotation rails, callout arrows or colourbars do the labelling instead [geometry.legend].
Figure 9 is the only colourbar in the paper and it prints one per panel (ticks 0, 0.5, 1), inside the right edge of each frame, with no colourbar anywhere else [geometry.colorbar].
Nothing is drawn in three dimensions: no perspective bars, no surface mesh, no isometric frame, in a paper whose subject is a value surface over land area [geometry.three_d].

Printed numbers are thin and uneven: Figures 1, 2 and 5 print a full tick set on both axes; Figures 4, 8 and 10 print ONE labelled y value each (5000, 5000, and 2000 with 4000) beside two to four x values; Figure 9 prints coordinates with no unit; the two photographs print none at all [geometry.printed_numbers].

Five exhibits carry text drawn inside the art and it is load-bearing: the K-sign annotation rails of Figures 1 and 2, the two callout arrows of Figure 4, the three boxed coordinate pairs of Figure 5, and the 'Figure (a)'/'(b)' labels under Figure 3's photographs [geometry.data_labels].

All ten captions print BELOW their art - there is no exhibit in this paper with a caption above it, and no table to establish the figure/table split this lane has recorded since #167 [caption.position].

The caption form is `Figure <n>: <label>` with a colon, a capitalised label, no terminal period and six to eighteen words; the numbering is uniform across all ten, so no exhibit is captioned without a number [caption.numbering].

NOT ONE OF THE TEN CAPTIONS CARRIES A FINITE VERB, A UNIT, A CONDITION OR A CONCLUSION: they are noun phrases and gerund stubs ('Applying the model to the steel production case', 'Positive initial system (+E(A))', 'Air pollution in Shanghai'), so voice is unassignable throughout and the caption never states what the exhibit shows [caption.voice].

Only the two coefficient-set captions name a variable, and they name it as the condition rather than as the axis ('(+E(A))', '(-E(A))'); no caption names an axis, a unit or a parameter value, and the parameter values that matter (K = 5000, C0 = 0.002) live in the prose [caption.variables].

Eight of the ten captions are quoted from the text layer; Figure 7's is TYPED FROM THE CROP because the layer prints 'Shanghui' where the page prints 'Shanghai' - a substitution rather than a truncation, which is a break mode the lane has not recorded before [caption.verbatim].

Citation is the weakest in the lane: only Figures 4, 5 and 8 are ever named by number in the prose, Figures 1, 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10 are never named at all, and Figure 3 is named once - on the page where it is NOT the exhibit under discussion [mention.count].

The one cross-reference to Figure 3 sits inside the panda case: 'May(Figure 3)' points the reader at the Kubuqi satellite photograph while the sentence is describing a giant panda distribution study, which is Figure 9 - a wrong-exhibit pointer, not a missing one [mention.style].

Pointer form where it exists is the verb-in-the-sentence kind: 'From Figure 4 above we can see that...', 'From Figure 5, we can see that...', 'As shown in Figure 8, ...'; the two unnamed exhibits are reached by deixis ('Based on the cost-beneﬁt stacked column chart above') or by citation alone ('according to a prediction research ... conducted in 2017,') [mention.lead_pattern].
Every pointer is same-page: no exhibit is named before the page it is printed on, and none is named later than its own page, so lead timing is zero throughout [mention.lead_pages].

Three exhibits are read in the sentence that follows (Figures 4, 5, 8) and the reading is a direction or a derivative ('the total value of this project decreases with increasing land-use area'), never a value taken off the axis; the other seven are never read at all [mention.trail_sentence].

Exhibits are allocated by stage of argument: the typology section takes the two mirror coefficient-set charts (Figures 1 and 2), the desert case takes a borrowed photo plus three model charts (Figures 3 to 6), the steel case one photo plus one chart (7, 8) and the reserve one borrowed map plus one chart (9, 10) [place.section_kind].
One page carries two exhibits (p11: Figures 5 and 6); the other eight exhibit pages carry one each, no exhibit owns a page, and none is landscape [place.page_order].

Region areas run from 0.0648 (Figure 4) to 0.2017 (Figure 9); six of the ten are under 0.13, and the two borrowed rasters (Figures 3 and 9) are the two largest, which inverts the paper's own emphasis - the model's curves are drawn small and the cited pictures are printed big [place.area_frac].
Document order equals number order throughout, and the numbering runs unbroken from 1 to 10 across four sections and two case studies [place.doc_order].

The text layer is corrupted in three ways that cost a transcription: the Shanghai/'Shanghui' substitution above, the split of Net(A) into 'N et(A)' in equation (14), and a completely missing x tick label in Figure 5 where the frame clips '14' off 14000 - the last of which is a PRINT defect the layer reproduces faithfully [caption.verbatim].
